title: Vikings’ 22-point fourth-quarter eruption stuns Packers, but how concerning is Kyler Murray’s injury?
content:
MINNEAPOLIS — The Minnesota Vikings overcame the loss of starting quarterback Kyler Murray and scored three fourth-quarter touchdowns to shock the Green Bay Packers 39-22 on Sunday. The Vikings scored 22 points in just 2:42 of game time to take the lead — and then pad it.

Penalties on three consecutive third downs gave Minnesota vital first downs on their go-ahead drive, which culminated in an Aaron Jones touchdown run with 6:37 remaining.

On the subsequent Packers possession, several Minnesota players converged to sack Jordan Love deep in Green Bay territory, and Andrew Van Ginkel ripped the ball out of Love’s hands as he was falling. On the next play, the Vikings scored on a Jordan Mason touchdown plunge.

Three plays later, Love’s pass was intercepted by James Pierre and returned to the Packers’ 14-yard line. Three plays later, Justin Jefferson’s incredible individual effort got him into the end zone for the second time on the day. The star wideout ended up with eight receptions for 92 yards and the two scores.

Murray, making his first start since joining the Vikings this offseason, was knocked out of the game in the first quarter after taking a violent hit to the head during a scramble. Murray was quickly ruled out and is in the concussion protocol.

The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman and Alec Lewis share their takeaways.

It isn’t clear yet if Murray will have to miss any time, the Vikings signed Carson Wentz for this exact reason. Murray had only played more than 11 regular-season games once in the last four seasons. Wentz offers knowledge of the system. Coach Kevin O’Connell trusts him to target Jefferson, which is perhaps the most important offensive priority.

And on Sunday, Wentz proved all of it. He orchestrated multiple touchdown drives, completing 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns. Jefferson caught two of them.

Wentz, though, is a backup for a reason. He has trouble surveying the field and frequently puts his body in harm’s way in the pocket. He has been injury-prone throughout his career, which places the Vikings in a precarious position, especially if Murray is out for an extended period of time.

This adds responsibility for third-year quarterback J.J. McCarthy, whom the Vikings demoted from starter in 2025 to third string in a span of an offseason. Minnesota didn’t trust McCarthy enough to make him the backup. If he is forced into that role, the Vikings will have to make sure he’s prepared. His injury history, too, adds another dimension for Minnesota. The team could also look to supplement its roster with another free-agent quarterback to cover for further depth issues. — Alec Lewis, Vikings beat writer

The Packers offense torched the Vikings defense for numerous explosive plays throughout Sunday’s game. Green Bay led 19-10 at halftime.

But Minnesota defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ unit flipped the script in the second half. In the fourth quarter, Flores’ group forced two Packers turnovers (the aforementioned Love fumble and interception) and stopped them twice more on downs. The pass rush engulfed Green Bay’s offensive line and swarmed Love.

The game turned when Packers coach Matt LaFleur took three points off the board early in the fourth quarter to attempt a fourth-and-1 at the Vikings’ 17. The Minnesota defense stopped Love on a sneak, and from that point on, the defense was smothering, applying pressure at the perfect time. Minnesota pressured Love on 13 snaps in the second half, sacking him four times, and left the Packers all out of sorts. — Lewis

We’ve all seen this movie before. The Packers have now blown double-digit, second-half leads in their last three meaningful games against NFC North opponents (Week 18 against the Vikings last season doesn’t count because the starters were rested with the No. 7 seed already secured).

Green Bay talked all offseason about finishing games better after collapsing late too many times last year, but the first game this season suggested that little has changed. On one play, the Packers played conservatively and ran for a 1-yard toss on third-and-12 early in the third quarter while leading 19-10. On another, they decided to be aggressive and take a field goal (and an eight-point lead) off the board, unsuccessfully sneaking Jordan Love on fourth-and-1. Those two plays hint at indecision from coach Matt LaFleur, which isn’t the most inspiring sign for this fan base after how last season fell apart. — Matt Schneidman, Packers beat writer

The Packers need to sort out their offensive line. Maybe Sunday’s leaky performance was simply a byproduct of facing Flores’ chaotic pressure packages, but Love was on his back far too much for Green Bay’s offense to flourish. There were mistakes across the line, from missed assignments in pass protection to pre-snap penalties, and they forced Love to operate off schedule, which made him less effective outside the pocket. Starting left guard Aaron Banks missed another game due to injury, this a knee issue that has nagged him all summer. He needs to get healthy, and those around him need to tighten things up, or this could be a long season for what should otherwise be a prolific passing attack. — Schneidman
